newsitem.title: INDONESIA: RTRS-Indonesia wants Bre-X to solve dispute.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Indonesia wants Bre-X to solve dispute.

text.p: Indonesia's director general of mining said on Wednesday the government would not interfere in a dispute between Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd and an Indonesian associate over a massive gold deposit in Kalimantan.
"We want them to settle the dispute between themselves and we cannot interfere in this case...because this is purely an internal company matter," Kuntoro Mangusubroto told Reuters.

Australian gold explorer Golden Valley Mines NL said this week it had entered into a technical and finance pact with Indonesian group PT Krueng Gasui, which has a 10 percent stake in Bre-X's Busang gold discovery in Kalimantan.
Golden Valley said PT Krueng had entered a deal with Bre-X in 1987 that gives it a call option over a further 20 percent in Bre-X's unit that controls the Busang deposit.
But, Bre-X said on Tuesday there is no evidence of a written agreement to support PT Krueng's claims.
"After they state they have solved the dispute, only then will we process the contract of work," Mangusubroto said.

Bre-X requires the contracts of work to further explore and develop the Busang II and III sections of what is believed to be one of the world's major gold deposits with current reserves estimated by the company of at least 47 million ounces.

Jusuf Merukh, the local Bre-X partner in Busang I with a 20 percent stake in the section through his two companies, told Reuters on Wednesday he also has a 20 percent stake in Busang II and III, where the richest deposits lie.
In addition, he said he had an option to buy a further 20 percent in all three sections.
Bre-X said its Indonesian legal adviser had advised it that the claims of its Indonesian partner was without merit.
